Guardian contract (machine-readable front matter — parsed by the Guardian pipeline) ```yaml guardian_issue: id: "OSS-CATALOG-SUBSET-VERIFIER" title: "Adopt `rigorix-verifier::verify_catalog_subset` — drop the inline subset re-check" epic: "server mode — C: catalog → servers → clients (D-3)" status: planned priority: low created_at: "2026-09-25T00:00:00Z" dependencies: - name: "SDK-VERIFIER-PUBLISH (rigorix-sdk #19)" type: cross-repo note: "The guard must be a published crate before OSS can take a dependency on it." - name: "OSS-CATALOG-SUBSET (rigorix-oss #905, merged #906)" type: internal note: "The subset relation is already correct inline; this replaces it with the shared implementation." intent: | #906 replaced the OSS catalog-parity equality assertion with an inline subset check, with a documented justification: `rigorix-verifier` is a private cross-repo crate, so a path/git dev-dependency would break the publishable public OSS build. Once `rigorix-verifier` is published to crates.io (SDK-VERIFIER-PUBLISH), that justification disappears — adopt the shared `verify_catalog_subset` so there is ONE implementation of the closed-namespace relation (no drift between the OSS inline copy and the SDK/enterprise guard). in_scope: - "Add `rigorix-verifier` as a DEV-dependency of `rigorix-server` (crates.io version, NOT path/git)." - "In `server/tests/catalog_parity.rs`, replace the local `undeclared_methods` helper + membership loop with `rigorix_verifier::verify_catalog_subset(&oss_names)`." - "Keep everything else in that test file: the field-drift check (auth/mcpTool), the negative test, the OSS-omits-`auth.verify` assertion, the MCP 1:1 mapping, and the D10 no-raw-step test." - "Keep the CI conformance step (`ci.yml` runs `catalog_parity oss_catalog_is_a_subset_of_the_sdk_catalog` with `RIGORIX_SDK_SCHEMAS`)." - "Update the test module header to note the shared guard (remove the 'private crate' justification)." out_of_scope: - "The enterprise guard (ENT-CATALOG-SUBSET-GUARD)." - "Any change to the catalog content." affected_layers: server: - "modify: server/Cargo.toml (dev-dependency: rigorix-verifier)" - "modify: server/tests/catalog_parity.rs (use verify_catalog_subset)" ci: - "no change expected (the step already uses RIGORIX_SDK_SCHEMAS)" canonical_references: - adr: "rigorix-sdk docs/adr/ADR-0001-native-api-catalog.md (D3)" - code: "rigorix-oss server/tests/catalog_parity.rs (the inline `undeclared_methods`); rigorix-sdk rust/rigorix-verifier/src/lib.rs::verify_catalog_subset" - precedent: "rigorix-oss #906 (the merged inline version + its documented deviation)" acceptance_criteria: - "[ ] `rigorix-server` dev-depends on the PUBLISHED `rigorix-verifier` (no path/git dep)" - "[ ] `oss_catalog_is_a_subset_of_the_sdk_catalog` calls `verify_catalog_subset`; no local `undeclared_methods` remains" - "[ ] The negative behaviour is still proven (an undeclared method fails)" - "[ ] `cargo test --workspace` green for a fresh public clone (no private-repo dependency)" - "[ ] CI green (fmt · clippy · test)" validators: [ci, tests, architecture, canonical] implementation_notes: | - Dev-dependency only — the server does not use the verifier at runtime. - Publishable-build constraint (the reason #906 deviated) must still hold: a crates.io version dependency is fine for a public crate; a `path =`/`git =` is not. - Watch the transitive version lines: the verifier uses `hmac 0.12` / `sha2 0.10` while the OSS workspace uses `0.13` / `0.11`. A dev-dep will build both; acceptable, but decide whether to align the verifier's versions first. - If the SDK instead chooses to expose the relation only via the JSON corpus (no crate), keep the inline check and close this as won't-do — but the preference is one impl. file_changes: - "modify: server/Cargo.toml" - "modify: server/tests/catalog_parity.rs" pipeline_steps: [implement, validate, create-mr, merge] ```
# OSS-CATALOG-SUBSET-VERIFIER: adopt the shared subset guard ## Problem #906 (merged) fixed the OSS catalog-parity test to a **subset** relation, but re-implemented the relation inline (`undeclared_methods` + a membership loop) rather than calling `rigorix-verifier::verify_catalog_subset`. The documented reason was sound at the time: `rigorix-verifier` is a private cross-repo crate, and a path/git dev-dependency would break the publishable public OSS build. ## What changed Once `rigorix-verifier` is published to crates.io (SDK-VERIFIER-PUBLISH / rigorix-sdk #19), the constraint is gone — a crates.io dev-dependency is fine for a public crate. Adopting the shared guard removes the OSS/SDK/enterprise duplication of the closed-namespace relation. ## Canonical references - ADR-0001 (D3) · `server/tests/catalog_parity.rs` (inline `undeclared_methods`) · `rust/rigorix-verifier/src/lib.rs::verify_catalog_subset` ## Acceptance Criteria | # | Criterion | Verify in | |---|-----------|-----------| | 1 | Dev-dep on the PUBLISHED verifier (no path/git) | review | | 2 | Test calls `verify_catalog_subset`; no inline helper | review | | 3 | Negative case still proven | unit | | 4 | Public clone `cargo test` green | CI | | 5 | CI green | CI |
title: OSS-CATALOG-SUBSET-VERIFIER: adopt `rigorix-verifier::verify_catalog_subset` (drop the inline re-check)

Guardian contract (machine-readable front matter) ```yaml guardian_issue: id: "OSS-AUDIT-C" title: "Audit integrity Phase C (OSS): anchored mode — rigorix-server anchor client + AnchoredHistoryAdapter + fail-closed" epic: "audit integrity (ADR-016)" status: planned priority: high dependencies: - "ADR-016 (rigorix-oss PR #897)" - "OSS-AUDIT-A (local chain + mode tagging + the ExecutionHistory port usage)" - "ENT-AUDIT-B (the ledger that anchors)" - "#888 OSS-C2 (rigorix-server — the host that will carry the anchor client)" intent: | Turn the guarantee on (ADR-016 Phase C). With the ledger (Phase B) in place, the OSS host gains an **anchor client** and a second `ExecutionHistory` implementation — `AnchoredHistoryAdapter` — that verifies the anchor's signature before the matcher sees any evidence. In anchored mode the guard reads authenticated history, and consequential runs **fail closed** when the anchor is unreachable. This is where the cross-run rules stop being best-effort and become a real control. in_scope: - "Anchor client in `rigorix-server`: push envelopes (carrying `producer_id`/`sequence`/`prev_hash`) to the ledger, and fetch a **signed history slice** for the current scope/window" - "`AnchoredHistoryAdapter` behind the existing `ExecutionHistory` port: verify the anchor's **Ed25519** signature over the slice (against a configured public key) before returning `prior_actions`; a forged/invalid slice fails closed" - "Mode selection: `local_unanchored` (no anchor configured — Phase A behavior) vs `anchored` (anchor configured, signature verified)" - "Tag envelopes `history_integrity = anchored`; carry the verified anchor `head_hash`/sequence into the envelope so a verdict is bound to a ledger head" - "Fail-closed: in anchored mode, a consequential (history-dependent / deny-class) run is REFUSED when the anchor is unreachable or returns an unverifiable slice" - "`rigorix.system.version` reports `history_integrity` + the anchor identity/head; config for the anchor endpoint + the anchor public key" - "Tests: forged slice rejected; unreachable anchor refuses a consequential run; reachable anchor allows; local_unanchored path unchanged" out_of_scope: - "The ledger itself (ENT-AUDIT-B)" - "Local tamper-evidence (OSS-AUDIT-A)" - "Phase D (trusted execution boundary / enclave / anchor-side observation)" - "Non-consequential runs: they may proceed when the anchor is down (they do not read authenticated history)" affected_layers: application: - "new: engine/.../sequence_policy/infrastructure/history_anchored.rs — AnchoredHistoryAdapter (verifies the slice)" - "modify: ExecutionHistory wiring / composition to select the adapter by mode" infrastructure: - "new: server/src/anchor/ (client: push + fetch; Ed25519 verify)" interfaces: - "modify: server `rigorix.system.version` — report history_integrity + anchor head" - "modify: server config — anchor endpoint + public key" composition: - "modify: server/backend.rs + mcp/src/host (mode-aware history adapter)" tests: - "new: forged-slice, unreachable-anchor, mode-switch tests" canonical_references: - adr: "rigorix-oss ADR-016 (Modes, Ownership, Validation #4 + #8, Phase C)" - code: "engine/src/sequence_policy/application/service.rs (ExecutionHistory port), engine/src/sequence_policy/infrastructure/history.rs (EnvelopeHistoryAdapter — Phase A)" - code: "server/ (from #888 PR A–E: dispatch, events), mcp/src/host (composition)" - schema: "SDK history-slice schema; rust/rigorix-verifier (anchor signature verification)" - issue: "ENT-AUDIT-B (the anchor), #888 (rigorix-server)" acceptance_criteria: - "[ ] A **forged** history slice is rejected before matching (signature verified)" - "[ ] In anchored mode, a consequential run is REFUSED when the anchor is unreachable (fail closed); a non-consequential run is unaffected" - "[ ] In anchored mode, a valid signed slice allows the run and the envelope records the verified head + `history_integrity = anchored`" - "[ ] `local_unanchored` behavior is unchanged when no anchor is configured" - "[ ] `rigorix.system.version` reports the active mode + anchor identity/head" - "[ ] The adapter swap happens **behind the existing port** — the matcher is unchanged (no sequence-policy logic added)" - "[ ] CI green; fmt/clippy -D warnings clean" validators: [ci, tests, security, architecture, canonical] implementation_notes: | - This is an **adapter swap**, not a matcher change: `ExecutionHistory` is already the seam. If you find yourself editing matching logic, stop — the design keeps the engine as the single evaluator. - Verify BEFORE matching: the adapter must reject an invalid signature and fail closed; never hand unverified facts to the matcher. - Fail-closed is mode-scoped: only consequential (history-dependent) runs in `anchored` mode. Everything else keeps working when the anchor is down. - The host holds only the anchor's **public** key — no host-side private key (that is Phase D). - Bind the verdict to the head: recording the verified `head_hash`/sequence in the envelope is what lets an auditor later prove which ledger state a decision used. file_changes: - "create: engine/src/sequence_policy/infrastructure/history_anchored.rs" - "create: server/src/anchor/" - "modify: server/src/backend.rs, server config, rigorix.system.version" - "modify: mcp/src/host (mode-aware wiring)" - "create: tests (forged slice / unreachable anchor / mode switch)" pipeline_steps: [implement, validate, create-mr, merge] ```
# OSS-AUDIT-C: Audit integrity Phase C (OSS) — anchored mode ## Intent Turn the guarantee on. With the ledger (Phase B), the OSS host gains an anchor client and an `AnchoredHistoryAdapter` that **verifies the anchor's signature before the matcher sees evidence**. In anchored mode consequential runs **fail closed** when the anchor is unreachable. Here the cross-run rules stop being best-effort and become a real control. ## In Scope - Anchor client in `rigorix-server` (push envelopes; fetch signed history slice). - `AnchoredHistoryAdapter` behind `ExecutionHistory`; Ed25519 verify before matching. - Modes: `local_unanchored` (Phase A) vs `anchored`; envelope tagged + head bound. - Fail-closed for consequential runs when the anchor is down. - `rigorix.system.version` reports the mode + anchor head. ## Out of Scope - The ledger (B), local tamper-evidence (A), Phase D. Non-consequential runs keep working without the anchor. ## Canonical References - **ADR-016** (Modes, Ownership, Validation #4/#8, Phase C) - `engine/src/sequence_policy/application/service.rs` (`ExecutionHistory`), `.../infrastructure/history.rs` (Phase A adapter) - `server/` (#888), SDK history-slice schema, `rigorix-verifier` - ENT-AUDIT-B ## Acceptance Criteria | # | Criterion | Verify in | |---|-----------|-----------| | 1 | Forged slice rejected before matching | unit | | 2 | Unreachable anchor refuses a consequential run (anchored) | integration | | 3 | Valid slice allows; envelope records head + mode | integration | | 4 | `local_unanchored` unchanged | regression | | 5 | `system.version` reports mode + head | unit | | 6 | Matcher unchanged (adapter swap only) | review | | 7 | CI green | CI | ## Implementation Notes - Adapter swap, not a matcher change. If you edit matching logic, stop. - Verify **before** matching; never pass unverified facts to the matcher. - Fail-closed is **mode-scoped** — only consequential runs in `anchored` mode. - Host holds only the **public** key (Phase D adds host-side signing). ## DoD - [ ] Anchor client + `AnchoredHistoryAdapter` landed; signature verified pre-match - [ ] Mode-scoped fail-closed + `system.version` reporting - [ ] Forged/unreachable/mode-switch tests green; CI green
title: OSS-AUDIT-C: Audit integrity Phase C — anchored mode (anchor client + AnchoredHistoryAdapter + fail-closed)
